name: azeroth-unbound

target.core: AzerothCore WotLK; exact Campaign Party revision not supplied
target.party: one controlled character plus up to four Playerbots

non_negotiable_constraints: Reuse assets and mechanics already in the 3.3.5a client; no new models or textures.
AzerothCore remains authoritative for levels, items, quests, skills, inventory and rewards.
Playerbots remain responsible for bot movement, combat and execution.
Campaign Party remains authoritative for party selection, permissions and command routing.
Never assume ownership of or overwrite an existing custom MPQ.
Asset IDs, database effects and gameplay remain unverified until qualified against supplied target data.

source_snapshot.note: Public upstream master source inspected for capability boundaries; this is not a pin for Campaign Party.

capability_assessments.fantasy: Unlock ordinary flying mounts over the outdoor zones of Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms, while keeping interiors, dungeons and intentional no-fly story spaces grounded.
capability_assessments.earliest_delivery: client+server AreaTable.dbc delta plus server policy hook; reuse existing mount visuals
capability_assessments.client_patch: required for zones whose AreaTable row is not flyable; DBC parity required
hard_limits: The stock AzerothCore check reads AREA_FLAG_OUTLAND before consulting the PlayerScript zone hook, so the hook alone cannot grant flight in non-flyable zones.
Keep AREA_FLAG_NO_FLY_ZONE and use a reviewed outdoor-zone allowlist; do not blanket-enable every area.
Client handling, collision, roofs, transports, anticheat and bot follow behavior require runtime qualification.
capability_assessments.evidence: UPSTREAM_SOURCE_PATH_INSPECTED; target revision, DBC records, client and Playerbots NOT_ASSESSED

capability_assessments.fantasy: A campaign-earned Frostmourne echo and Lich King-inspired plate regalia become a personalized, level-scaling endgame chase rather than GM-only curiosities.
capability_assessments.earliest_delivery: new server item entries; add matching Item.dbc records only if no reusable item row already has the verified display/class/slot; reuse existing display IDs and frost effects
capability_assessments.client_patch: conditional DBC rows; no new M2/BLP
hard_limits: Do not invent ItemDisplayInfo IDs. Search supplied local DBCs and trace their dependent assets.
A creature/NPC appearance is not automatically a wearable ItemDisplayInfo appearance; if the exact armor display is absent, kitbash a verified stock wearable set.
WotLK has no stock transmog system: the item must equip in a real slot or be presented as a separate cosmetic illusion with its own supported mechanism.
capability_assessments.patch_cost: none if a usable Item.dbc row and display already exist; otherwise DBC rows; no new art
capability_assessments.evidence: ENGINE_MECHANISM_SOURCE_BACKED; candidate stock appearance IDs NOT_ASSESSED

capability_assessments.fantasy: A level-18 hero can follow the same world-spanning campaign through Duskwood, Tanaris or Grizzly Hills; the local wildlife remains a fair challenge instead of becoming gray scenery.
capability_assessments.earliest_delivery: compiled server module with a deterministic scaling policy; reuse zone creatures, spawns and stock stats
capability_assessments.client_patch: not inherently required for creatures; item rows may separately need Item.dbc
hard_limits: The source hook runs when a creature selects its level, before base stats are generated; it is not proof of a working module.
Keep level results within available CreatureBaseStats and content-specific bounds.
Choose a party anchor, clamp bosses, and do not change a live combat encounter when another character arrives.
Quest reward and quest-level scaling are separate problems; use verified, normalized campaign currencies until those paths are tested.
capability_assessments.patch_cost: server module/config; no client patch for reused creatures; no new art
capability_assessments.evidence: ENGINE_HOOK_SOURCE_BACKED; balance, party selection, bot levels and compiled behavior NOT_ASSESSED

capability_assessments.fantasy: Let the player choose any discovered region for the next campaign chapter; story progression follows evidence, alliances and choices, not an imposed level corridor.
capability_assessments.earliest_delivery: world SQL, scripts and optional 3.3.5a addon; existing zones/NPCs/objects
capability_assessments.client_patch: none for server-authored quest text and reused assets; local asset check still required
hard_limits: Quest graph, breadcrumb admission, character persistence and party/altbot quest semantics need explicit tests.
A quest log is not an unlimited narrative database; keep optional branches in server-owned records and present summaries through supported UI.
capability_assessments.patch_cost: server SQL/module; optional addon folder; no new art

capability_assessments.fantasy: Add Cartography or Relicwright as a world-exploration vocation: discover, record and restore ancient sites, using the existing Material Exchange as an adapter rather than replacing professions or inventory.
capability_assessments.earliest_delivery: either a true client-visible profession with SkillLine/SkillRaceClassInfo/SkillLineAbility DBC records and server spells, or a no-slot server-side vocation presented in an addon
capability_assessments.client_patch: true skill profession requires DBC rows and stock icon reuse; sidecar vocation can avoid skill-line DBC edits
hard_limits: Upstream config documents a maximum of 11 primary profession slots; this raises the cap, it does not create a skill line or recipes.
A genuine profession needs client skill-line data, eligibility rows, abilities, spells, recipes and UI acceptance.
A sidecar vocation must not silently consume primary-profession slots or replace Campaign Party's Material Exchange.
capability_assessments.patch_cost: DBC rows for a true profession; server module/addon only for sidecar vocation; no new art

capability_assessments.fantasy: Connect remote campaign sites through existing taxi routes, ships and zeppelins; a recovered skyway becomes a meaningful reward before unrestricted flight is earned.
capability_assessments.earliest_delivery: world SQL/config and reused transport models/routes; DBC rows only for genuinely new client-visible taxi nodes
capability_assessments.client_patch: none for reused routes; conditional DBC for new taxi nodes/routes
hard_limits: Playerbot boarding/follow and cross-map handoff must be qualified; a visual transport is not proof that bots can ride it.
Never add fake taxi nodes without matching client data.
capability_assessments.patch_cost: none or DBC rows depending on whether routes/nodes are reused; no new art
capability_assessments.evidence: REUSE_PATTERN_SOURCE_DOCUMENTED; target route inventory and bot operation NOT_ASSESSED

capability_assessments.fantasy: Every week a different region becomes an active front: towns change phase, patrols move, rare leaders appear, and campaign choices alter which faction controls the next objective.
capability_assessments.earliest_delivery: server SQL plus event/module logic; reuse stock creature and gameobject displays
hard_limits: game_event.eventEntry is a tinyint; reserve only 1-255 after checking the target database.
Per-character choices need durable server state; world-global effects can expose one player's progress to others unless phased or instanced.
capability_assessments.patch_cost: server SQL/module; no client patch; no new art
capability_assessments.evidence: MECHANIC_SOURCE_BACKED_IN_REPOSITORY; concurrency, persistence and live event tests NOT_ASSESSED

capability_assessments.fantasy: Revisit familiar 3.3.5 dungeons as five-person memory echoes: rotating objectives, optional affixes, checkpoints after wipes and rewards that scale to the campaign band.
capability_assessments.earliest_delivery: server module + SQL in existing instance maps; reuse all environment and creature assets
capability_assessments.client_patch: none unless a new client-visible spell/item row is required
hard_limits: Dynamic scaling and loot must be tested for one controlled character plus four actual Playerbots, not just five human players.
Recoverable wipes, lockouts, loot ownership and bot interrupts/healing are separate acceptance gates.
capability_assessments.evidence: REUSE_PATTERN; encounter and Playerbots behavior NOT_ASSESSED

capability_assessments.fantasy: A legendary item remembers the world: its name, proc cadence and campaign title evolve when the player completes regional chapters, while stats remain bounded to the current character level.
capability_assessments.earliest_delivery: server-side upgrade stages represented by distinct validated item templates and quest states; reuse a verified item appearance and spell visual
capability_assessments.client_patch: conditional Item.dbc row for each distinct item identity; no patch if a supported existing identity can be reused safely
hard_limits: Avoid silently mutating a player's owned item or bypassing AzerothCore ownership; stage upgrades as explicit server-validated item exchanges.
Proc balance and triggered-spell recursion need server tests.
capability_assessments.patch_cost: server SQL/module plus conditional DBC rows; no new art
capability_assessments.evidence: MECHANIC_SOURCE_BACKED; feature behavior and assets NOT_ASSESSED

capability_assessments.fantasy: Turn exploration into a detective game: discover landmarks, inspect old-world relics, piece together clues and unlock optional branches without forcing the character to level in a particular zone.
capability_assessments.earliest_delivery: world SQL/module and optional addon; reuse existing books, objects, icons and map APIs available to 3.3.5a
capability_assessments.client_patch: none if existing assets are reused
hard_limits: Map API and addon calls must be checked against the 3.3.5a interface, not modern retail examples.
Clue state is server-owned; client map pins are only a presentation cache.
capability_assessments.patch_cost: server SQL/module; optional addon folder; no new art

flagship_campaign.title: The Atlas of Unfinished Wars
flagship_campaign.premise: A survey order discovers that old-world conflicts are connected by a network of abandoned skyways and relic sites. The player can start in any unlocked region; evidence, not level, advances the story.
flagship_campaign.chapter_order: player-selected among available regions; finale admission checks a short list of campaign proofs, not a mandatory leveling route

chapters.title: The Map That Lies
chapters.loop: Choose a frontier, investigate a local mystery, return with a clue; enemies scale within a declared band.

chapters.title: Roads Above the Ruins
chapters.loop: Restore reused taxi/transport links and earn a flight charter; old-world flight is gated by the separate DBC + server policy work.

chapters.title: The King's Last Shadow
chapters.loop: Recover verified relic appearances and decide whether to bind a Frostmourne echo or dismantle it; no exact stock display IDs are presumed.

chapters.title: Five Against the Echo
chapters.loop: Run a bot-operable memory encounter with interrupts, tank swaps, healer thresholds, hazards and a recoverable checkpoint.

chapters.title: A World That Remembers
chapters.loop: A scheduled living front reflects campaign choices; optional branches and collection rewards remain repeatable.

flagship_campaign.reward_contract: AzerothCore validates quest completion and item ownership. Rewards use deterministic campaign identities, explicit upgrade exchanges and level-banded stock scaling; Material Exchange is called through an adapter and remains authoritative downstream.
flagship_campaign.status: DESIGN_ONLY; not valid Foundry spec; no generated gameplay claims
